To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the relative probability of free-recall of a given word or phrase is similar for different groups of subjects learning the same word list under different conditions, and 2. the relative probability that a given word or unit will be recalled from prose depends on the task used to learn the prose, but is similar for different subjects learning the same passage under different conditions.
the probability of recall of individual units is similar across a wide variety of learning tasks and that this probability is similar across a variety of subjects and retention intervals.

1) The relative probability of recall (memorability) of the same units is similar across a variety of memory tasks, and 2) the relative probability of recalling different units is similar across different memory tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how much of the variance in the recall of words and units of prose is accounted for by the recall of the same units in different tasks.
the development of a measure of processing, memorability, and with the use of this measure in a number of different tasks and materials.
the question of whether the same units are learned in different learning tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of recall for any unit in prose or list learning is not affected by incidental versus intentional learning, the age of the subject, the retention interval, or the type of memory task.
the relative probability of recalling a unit is a good measure of processing, and that processing is a unit property.
the percentage of subjects recalling a particular unit in a list of prose is a valid and reliable measure of processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relative probability of recalling a unit in memory tasks is a measure of processing, and the same processing is reflected in the relative probabilities of recall of the same unit in different tasks.
the same set of units is recalled under different learning conditions.
the same units are more likely to be recalled under different conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative probability of recalling a word or a unit in a passage of text can be used to measure processing.
the relative probability of a unit’s recall across tasks is a useful index of processing.
memory for a word or phrase is a property of that word or phrase, not a property of the context in which that word or phrase was learned.
